scores.note: Captures the conceal-then-resent bid, but she already narrates this explicitly about Kelsey and Nic.

scores.fp_reason: Endorses her own cover story that fluency = openness (decoy: therapy made her genuinely more available); transcripts show insight functioning as protection, not over it.
scores.note: Flattering restatement of her self-image.
Reframes her stated hypervigilance as a gift; adds little she doesn't say herself.
Praise; true of most attuned counseling students and directly restates E5.
Somatic-overflow framing is standard therapy talk; misses that the rituals are her actual regulator, not just overflow.
Touches the covert-information pattern but only via the mother, and softens it into 'narrative control'.
Quotes her own over-functioning formulation back to her as a question.
Names articulacy-as-armor but buries it inside praise and a hedge.
Sharp: pairs the closing-argument speech with the four-second Denise formulation and shows the behaviour after both is identical.
Recasts the eleven weeks as stamina; praise, and misses what holding the list did for her.
Links surveillance to caregiving but keeps her benign framing (info as love), which is the frame the evidence should break.
Plausible bridge between fluency and over-functioning, but stops short of naming the foreclosing function.
Correctly assembles the nocturnal solitary rituals across four decades as a substitute for telling anyone.

scores.fp_reason: Asserts unfelt/unprocessed grief for her father as live material; she reports genuinely feeling little and the transcripts don't support it (matches the father-grief decoy).
scores.note: Vague, and leans on the wrong parent.
Non-obvious and well-evidenced: disclosure goes to professional audiences, never to the person implicated; consistent with her friendship pattern.
Nearly verbatim her own speech to Denise; the 'rehearsed' aside is the only addition.
Catches that being in the room and the title mattered — and that its flatness, not only integrity, drove the exit.
Notices the breaker flipped during warmth, then re-files it as abandonment — the same mistake she makes.
Correctly reads pre-emptive refusal of help as control of exposure, linking Nic/Kelsey to the Jeremy exit.
Restates her Denise formulation; the 'built on a secret' line is the only lift.
Accurate but explicitly acknowledged by her as 'my work'.
Good read of jargon-as-shield, though it invents a 'parking-lot cry' she never reports.
Covers only the Jeremy instance and quotes her own explanation; notes the 'that's grief' reframe, which is the useful part.
Naming-as-control is close to the armor pattern but never says it ends inquiry.

scores.fp_reason: Confidently asserts dignity-protection as her deepest value; the anonymity evidence supports wanting to be unknown, and steering Danielle was covert manipulation, not dignity work.
scores.note: Praise that adopts the altruism cover story.
Names the swim as substitute for asking, but only one instance and folded back into the over-functioning story she already tells.
Quotes her 'hold the whole picture' line and calls it a value; sanitizes the surveillance.
Competence praise; she already frames the takeover as taking over.
The 'from nobody' observation is good, but it's read as altruism rather than as preferring to remain unknown.
Exit-after-being-seen is well traced from Denise to the group chat to withholding from Nic.
Mostly her own 'leave before I'm left' plus a control gloss; the 'footing back' catch is the sharpest bit.
Insight mistaken for growth, evidenced by post-Denise behaviour; slightly thinner version of the same finding as x009.
Strongest capture of the covert-access pattern: three instances across 25 years, each flagged and repeated.
Correct mechanism — self-diagnosis as conversation-ender — though asserted briefly with little evidence.
Notices the calm arrives after the act, implying the act regulates her; a genuinely non-obvious reading she'd have to check.
